thread:
incident-bot: Paging: automated monitors flagged increased generation divergence correlated with KV prefix cache hits. Please acknowledge and join triage.

joel (oncall): Acking. I'm pulling logs. Which prefixes are noisy and any customer reports?

priya: Seeing spikes for prefixes in range 0x7d..0x8b. Symptoms: client edits applied but subsequent reads return previous state for ~15-45s. Repro when write bursts coincide with replication window.

sam: I can confirm, reproduced with stress test that issues surface when invalidation messages queue up. Seems to be a race between invalidation ack and read path.

incident-bot: Customers impacted: 4 enterprise tenants reporting >8% incorrect entity retention in last 10m. SLO alerting triggered.

joel (oncall): Immediate mitigations: (a) scoped disable prefix caching for the affected ranges, (b) apply moderate write throttles to high-churn tenants, (c) open customer comms. Priya/sam can infra enact the bypass?

infra-bot: Running toggle: `feature.flip prefix_cache_disable --ranges 7d-8b --scope region:global --reason "kv_invalidation_race"` Rolling to routing mesh now. ETA ~40s.

lina: Also pushing tenant write throttles: `rbctl tenant update --id tenant-78 --write-qps 2` and similar for top 6 churn tenants. Edge rate-limits for chat route added: `ratelimit: 50rpm` for heavy tenants.

priya: Deploy-bot just emitted a canary: `deploy-bot: canary deploy read-fallback v1.2.3 to canary1` This introduces a read-through check: if cached entry age > 200ms or invalidation in-flight, fetch direct from store. Adds ~20-40ms on those reads.

sam: Added quick verification probe to internal healthcheck:```bash
curl -s -X POST https://internal.redwood/v1/kv_check \ 
 -H 'Authorization: Bearer $INT' \ 
 -d '{"prefix":"0x7e","key":"probe-key","expect":"new-val"}'
```

customer-support: Status update sent to affected customers: "We're investigating inconsistent chat replies for some workloads. We've enabled targeted cache bypasses and throttled writes to reduce incidents. Engineering is deploying a safe read-fallback to prevent stale reads. No data loss. Will follow up with timeline." :email:

joel (oncall): Handoff: I'm going off-shift, handing to sam for next 90 minutes. Sam you own mitigations + RCA coordination.

sam: Taking over. Current mitigations list: bypass ranges 7d-8b active, write quotas reduced for 6 tenants, edge limits in place, read-fallback canary deployed to canary1. Monitoring dashboards: KV-invalidation-queue, cache-hit-age, customer-error-rate.

ops-lead: Can we prefer a gradual read-fallback roll rather than global bypass? Bypass removes cache benefits. If fallback looks stable in 30m, rollback bypass and enable fallback across regions.

priya: Agreed. Plan: monitor canary for 20m, if stale-read incidents drop and latency within acceptable bounds (<+50ms p95), expand to 25% traffic, then full roll. If regress, re-enable bypass and collect traces.

infra-bot: Propagated bypass to us-east-1 and us-west-2. eu-west-1 queued next; canary will be in eu-west-1 once deployed.

deploy-bot: `deploy status read-fallback v1.2.3: canary1 SUCCESS, canary2 PENDING`

sam: Quick note for RCA: likely root cause is out-of-order invalidation acknowledgements under replication lag when writes are batched. Action items: add per-prefix invalidation sequencing, surface invalidation lag metric, and add audit log for invalidation events per tenancy.

customer-support: Updating customers with follow-up: "We've activated temporary mitigations. Engineering will rollout a verification fallback to ensure reads are correct; we expect a resolution path within a few hours."

joel (oncall): Thanks everyone. If anything spikes, page me. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Handoff recorded: joel -> sam. Severity set to P2. Thread will be used for updates and final postmortem link."
